messages:
Carlos: Heads-up — us-west-2 rtx-8k pool queue depth jumped ~3x in the last 25m, per-model queues for gpt-open-13b are backing up. Latency SLOs starting to breach. Admission controller showing increased rejections/backpressure. Dashboard: https://go/replay/abc123 :warning:
Dana: Looking now, pulling logs and recent routing decisions.
Ben: Any idea if this is hosted traffic burst or Dedicated noisy neighbor?
Carlos: Mostly hosted. Two large customers spiking chat requests with long contexts (~8k). Also some retry storming after earlier 429s.
Alice: We have capacity-based rate limits but they’re pool-level only. Per-model shaping wasn't enabled for this pool — that could help.
infra-bot: ALERT: queue_depth(us-west-2-rtx8)>100 for 3m window; incident_id=inc-2026-1972
Ben: Can we enable per-model admission control and a soft fallback to quantized variants for low-tier keys? There's an ingress flag: `admission_policy.enable_model_shaping=true`.
Dana: I'll stage a route tweak to divert 20% of gpt-open-13b traffic to quantized-q4 variant and redirect another 20% to the t4 pool as a graceful degradation. Pushing change to canary.
Carlos: Note cost tradeoff — moving to t4 will increase egress and might raise per-token CPU time for long contexts. Also watch for tail latency. Are we okay with that to preserve SLOs?
Alice: Prioritize SLOs over cost for now. Notify support and sales of possible degraded quality. @Eve (support) can you prep a customer-facing note? :loudspeaker:
Eve (support): Will draft a short message asking affected customers to throttle heavy background jobs for the next 60–90 minutes.
Ben: Canary config I applied:
```yaml
routes:
  - match: model==gpt-open-13b
    weight: 60
  - match: model==gpt-open-13b
    variant: quantized-q4
    weight: 20
  - match: model==gpt-open-13b
    target_pool: us-west-2-t4
    weight: 20
```
deploy-bot: Rollout started for route change canary id=rout-canary-554 (20% shift)
Dana: Monitoring metrics — queue depth down ~40% after 10m, p95 latency trending back under target. No major error uptick so far.
Carlos: Good progress. Let's keep the canary for 30m then either promote or adjust. Opening backlog triage ticket and postmortem placeholder: https://go/issue/REDWOOD-3214. Add notes on auto-scale thresholds and per-model shaping defaults.
infra-oncall: I'll keep watch for 2h and escalate if queue depth rises again. If we see repeated patterns, recommend automatic temporary crediting or rate-limit enforcement at org-level.
Alice: Agreed. After this stabilizes, we should add a runbook step: enable per-model shaping for pools with mixed workloads and set default soft-fallback variants.
Carlos: Thanks all. Follow-ups: Dana (monitoring), Ben (postmortem config), Eve (customer comms).
